March !, 1999
Creative Writing

Avoiding my old hobby

As the slow and steady rain falls from the sky down onto the ground I am 
reminded of the sound of hot coffee perculating. I think about waking up to the aroma of 
my father's coffee as it slowly seeps beneath my door and finally reaches my nose.
---
Upon waking and gathering my senses another thought fills my head. If the morning coffee is ready it must be time for my waking routine of having a cup of hot java in one hand (with cream and sugar, of course) and a newly lit cigarette in the other. My life is just a series of routine after routine. It is my belief that each person's series of routines either makes or breaks their life, and makes up their lifestyle.

We are all creatures of habit, whether we like it or not. My unfortunate luck is that I always seem to get stuck with the bad habits rather than the good ones. You see, a majority of my bad habits, or routines, are all interconnected. Imagine a chain link fence or perhaps a sweater, each individual fabric or link holds all the others in place. Even if one or two individual structures are removed the form, or routine, will remain the same. This interconnectedness is what makes the structure, in my case the routine, the same. The coffee leads to a cigarette and the cigarette leads to an even greater evil: drugs and alcohol.

cards.typed_words:
Scan
WELLNESS
Tom Jensen
Health and Wellness
June 12, 2001
---
What is wellness? That is certainly a good question to start with when one is trying to decide how well one's well is. I would consider wellness the successful achievement of one limiting one's negative characteristics and traits. By limiting the negative in one's collective body and soul the effect, therefore, is accenting the positive. Addition by subtraction if you will. So, since coming to the very real acceptance of who I am and what I do I am able to make a judgment over how well is my wellness. What flaws have been noticed, studied, and fixed? What traits have I stepped back from my eyes and observed from another frame of reference? How have I felt about my relationships with friends and family? What have I yet to achieve on the Totem Pole of life, how far have I climbed? All things of this nature make for interesting talk and type but the main element one has to remember is that all of these subjects are subjective to the observer. Anyone may relate oneself to others in an attempt to compare actions and sometimes even justify an unjust act. One's immediate circle acts as the shell in which the egg is kept. On one hand, the shell can protect the egg from predators, harm and frying pans but the shell also succeeds in limiting how far the egg can expand and thereby cut off the egg from the far away chicken of happiness. I am the egg man, sorry Mr. Lennon.

But, as the more I learn the more I see how correct my poetry can be. It seems society has reached the point where it can no longer envision evil and therefore attempt to prevent evil from happening in the first place. It is only after

worthy.

COPING

Tom Jensen

June 10, 2001

Health and Wellness

That people get sick or experience unpleasant emotions in response to stress should come as no surprise. What may seem more surprising is that most people who experience life crises remain healthy. This resiliency in the face of
---
stress reflects the ways people deal with stressful situations, or ways of coping. 
Many coping strategies are consciously selected, whereas others, known as 
defense mechanisms, are largely unconscious. A study of women hospitalized 
while awaiting biopsies to determine whether or not they had breast cancer 
shows how variable coping responses can be. All thirty women were in the same 
potentially life-threatening situation, but their emotional responses and ability to 
function despite their anxiety varied considerably. One woman denied she had 
problem, blaming the lump on a fall in the bathtub. Another complained that her 
husband, not her, was the one who required medical attention. And still others 
drew on their religious faith to cope with their illness. 

Researchers often distinguish between three types of coping strategies: 
(1) efforts to change the situation, (2) efforts to alter one's cognition about the 
situation, and (3) efforts to alter the unpleasant emotional consequences of 
stress. In other words, if a person cannot change a stressful situation directly, he 
or she may try to change his or her perception of it or the emotion it endangers. 

Efforts to cope by changing the situation typically involve problem solving. 
The individual may try to remove the stressor, plan ways of resolving the 
situation, or seek advice or assistance from others in changing the situation.

A Hard Rain's Gonna Fall

The smoke from a half lit cigarette waves aimlessly through the air. A light brown guitar sits in the corner awaiting the delicate touch of its master. Three empty notebooks sit atop the table curiously wondering what will fill their blank pages. Will there be small sketches of beautiful young women or perhaps some silly verses about how everybody must get stoned? An old weathered, green chair, still feeling the pain of a dropped cigarette, reminisces about the time it's owner, the master, once sat for what seemed like an eternity trying to capture the soul of a man named Hollis Brown. An old, rusty razor lays, forgotten, in a corner clutching on to one last piece of cocaine. A broken guitar string sits beneath a pile of trash still humming the melody of what it prays comes true in "Forever Young", and in the state of mind that it will never be thrown away.

A familiar face appears from behind a closed door. All of the objects in the room experience a buzz of excitement. Perhaps one of them will receive their master's attention, if even only for an instant. The master sits upon the green chair and sighs. "Must be another sad love song", the chair thinks to itself. The razor, on the other hand says, "I think he's angry at the world, I hope he's not as angry as that 'Masters of war' song... You know, the one that goes:

I may be receiving a fancy Latin phrase and the same pretty whatever-colored tassel that my fellow English majors receive, but deep down inside I know that I am really a History major who just loves to write. I have had such sneaky suspicions before over taking this literary criticism course - though surveyish in its nature as it may be - but it has cemented my uncertainties into truths. Thank you Salem State English department.

Curious about what happens because of the Y2K bug? For a glimpse of the future stop by the computer lab in Meier Hall Room 210.

As you walk in, you briefly survey the scene. There are nine or ten students typing away on their keyboards  -  typing up reports and E-mailing their friends. cards.typed_words:
WELLNESS by Tom Jensen

What is wellness? That is certainly a good question to start with when one is trying to decide how well one's well is. I would consider wellness the successful achievement of one limiting one's negative characteristics and traits. By limiting the negative in one's collective body and soul the effect, therefore, is accenting the positive. Addition by subtraction if you will. So, since coming to the very real acceptance of who I am and what I do I am able to make a judgment over how well is my wellness. What flaws have been noticed, studied, and fixed? What traits have I stepped back from my eyes and observed from another frame of reference? How have I felt about my relationships with friends and family? What have I yet to achieve on the Totem Pole of life, how far have I climbed? All things of this nature make for interesting talk and type but the main element one has to remember is that all of these subjects are subjective to the observer. Anyone may relate oneself to others in an attempt to compare actions and sometimes even justify an unjust act. One's immediate circle acts as the shell in which the egg is kept. On one hand, the shell can protect the egg from predators, harm and frying pans but the shell also succeeds in limiting how far the egg can expand and thereby cut off the egg from the far away chicken of happiness. I am the egg man, sorry Mr. Lennon.

But, as the more I learn the more I see how correct my poetry can be. It seems society has reached the point where it can no longer envision evil and therefore attempt to prevent evil from happening in the first place. It is only after the original act has been done that the necessary corrections are deemed worthy.

Cannot fix the flaw - only patch the hole

I have had such sneaky suspicions before ever taking this literary criticism course  -  though surveyish in its nature as it may be  -  but it has cemented my uncertainties into truths. Thank you Salem State English Department.

When undertaking the discussion of literary criticism I am always sure to bring two tools with me: Number One- my dictionary, which helps me decipher such phrases as: spatiotemporal coordinates (P.552), concomitant utilization (P.549), and typical double-accented, double-styled hybrid construction (P. 426). Noah never intended this, but I digress... Number Two: my sleeping pills, which help me stay awaking during seemingly endless tirades over the Rule of Hyperdense Intertextuality as it applies to the assumption that any intertextual connection is interpretively relevant. because it provides a serene death, opposed to what could be weeks

terminally ill people who are suffering have the right to end their
